column2: the plan deduplicates final-summary emit instructions out of `skills/design/skill.md` but does not repoint `scripts/test-render-cost-line-callsites.sh` (and its `.md` sibling). `make lint` runs that harness, which greps `skills/design/skill.md` for exact strings the plan removes (e.g. `emit its full body verbatim as plain chat markdown`, step 0b `final_summary_path` gate, step 5d marker-extraction prose, `regardless of \`plan_write_ok\``, anti-halt `_publish_rc` gate). the refactor fails ci even when behavior is unchanged and ad-hoc plan greps pass.

step 0b cancel routes (`cancel-title-filter`, `cancel-reentry-guard`) today emit only via read when `${final_summary_path:-$design_tmpdir/final-summary.md}` is non-empty; they have no `design-step-final-summary.sh` or `design-step5c.sh` handoff and no marker-bearing background task. the proposed shared reference makes marker extraction from completed task output the primary path. pointing step 0b at the shared file without an explicit file-only carve-out can make the orchestrator scan unrelated prior tool output (e.g. route-wrapper stdout) for markers before the file fallback, changing cancel-route behavior versus today's line 271.

skills/shared/final-summary-emit.md:34-38 marker-first profile omits the in-context task-notification source rule that today's skill pins for background fences. scenario: the plan moves marker extraction into the shared file but only says to extract from the completed task output the caller names. current `skills/design/skill.md` (final summary block ~327) and step 5c abort (~879) require locating markers in the task-notification output already in the orchestrator context window, without a bash/python re-read. after dedup, an orchestrator can treat caller-named output as a file or log to re-open, which is forbidden by the no-tool-call rule yet is the only way to recover markers if the notification text is not named as the source. that risks missed markers, wrong-source extraction, or silent omission of the structured summary on `design-step-final-summary.sh` / `design-step5c.sh` paths.
